front: Picture: a tall, thin skeleton in a black pinstripe suit with a bat-shaped bow tie, standing before a huge full moon on a curling hill. He is known as the "Pumpkin King".
back: Jack Skellington, from Tim Burton's The Nightmare Before Christmas (1993, directed by Henry Selick). He is the Pumpkin King of Halloween Town.

front: Who gave Jack Skellington his speaking voice and his singing voice in The Nightmare Before Christmas?
back: Chris Sarandon did the speaking voice. Danny Elfman, who also wrote the songs, did the singing voice.

front: Picture: a small floating ghost dog with a glowing jack-o'-lantern nose, from The Nightmare Before Christmas.
back: Zero, Jack Skellington's ghost dog. His glowing pumpkin nose lights the way for Jack's sleigh, like Rudolph.

front: In The Nightmare Before Christmas, what holiday does Jack Skellington try to take over, and whom does he kidnap?
back: Christmas. He has Santa Claus kidnapped, calling him "Sandy Claws".

front: Picture: a blanket-clutching boy sitting alone in a moonlit pumpkin patch at night, waiting, while a girl in a coat sits next to him.
back: Linus van Pelt and Sally Brown waiting for the Great Pumpkin, in It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown (1966).

front: In what year did It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown first air, and on which network?
back: 1966, on CBS. Charles Schulz wrote it, Bill Melendez directed it, and Vince Guaraldi did the music.

front: In It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown, what does Linus believe the Great Pumpkin does?
back: He believes the Great Pumpkin rises out of the most "sincere" pumpkin patch on Halloween night and brings toys to children. Linus writes him a letter every year.

front: "I got a rock." Who says it, and in what special?
back: Charlie Brown, every time he is given a treat while trick-or-treating, in It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown (1966).

front: Picture: a beagle in a WWI flying helmet and goggles, sitting on top of his doghouse as if it were a plane, in a Halloween special.
back: Snoopy as the World War I Flying Ace, fighting the Red Baron, in It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown.

front: Picture: a glittering round orange-and-gold carriage shaped like a pumpkin, pulled by white horses, with a fairy godmother waving a wand.
back: Cinderella's pumpkin coach, from Disney's Cinderella (1950). The Fairy Godmother turns a pumpkin into the coach with "Bibbidi-Bobbidi-Boo."

front: At what time does Cinderella's coach turn back into a pumpkin?
back: At the stroke of midnight. The pumpkin was introduced in Charles Perrault's 1697 version of the story.

front: Picture: a 19th-century painting of a black-cloaked rider with no head, galloping on a black horse after a lanky schoolmaster through a dark forest.
back: The Headless Horseman chasing Ichabod Crane, from Washington Irving's The Legend of Sleepy Hollow. The painting is John Quidor's.

front: Who wrote The Legend of Sleepy Hollow, and in what collection was it published?
back: Washington Irving. It appeared in The Sketch Book of Geoffrey Crayon, Gent. (1820).

front: In The Legend of Sleepy Hollow, what does the Headless Horseman throw at Ichabod Crane at the bridge, and who is the suspected prankster?
back: A shattered pumpkin was found the next morning where Ichabod vanished. The suspected prankster is his rival Brom Bones, who was also courting Katrina Van Tassel.

front: Picture: an animated cartoon of a black horseman holding up a flaming, cackling jack-o'-lantern while a skinny man on a plow horse flees.
back: The Headless Horseman in Disney's The Adventures of Ichabod and Mr. Toad (1949). Bing Crosby narrates the Sleepy Hollow segment.

front: Who directed the 1999 film Sleepy Hollow, and who played Ichabod Crane and the Horseman?
back: Tim Burton directed it. Johnny Depp played Ichabod Crane, here a New York constable, and Christopher Walken played the Hessian Horseman.

front: Picture: a hulking, gray-brown, spindly demon with a large bulbous head, long fingers and a curved spine, stalking through a foggy rural night. It is also the title of a 1988 horror film.
back: Pumpkinhead (1988), the directorial debut of special-effects master Stan Winston.

front: In Pumpkinhead (1988), who summons the demon, and why?
back: Ed Harley, played by Lance Henriksen, has a witch summon it to take revenge on the teenagers who killed his young son by accident. The demon is dug up from a pumpkin patch graveyard.

front: Picture: a book illustration of a gangly figure with a stick-and-wooden body and a carved jack-o'-lantern for a head, wearing a pink shirt and a vest.
back: Jack Pumpkinhead, from L. Frank Baum's The Marvelous Land of Oz (1904).

front: In the Oz books, who built Jack Pumpkinhead, and how did he come to life?
back: The boy Tip built him, and Tip is later revealed to be Princess Ozma. The witch Mombi brought him to life with the Powder of Life.

front: Which 1985 Disney film brought Jack Pumpkinhead to the screen alongside Tik-Tok and the Gump?
back: Return to Oz (1985), starring Fairuza Balk as Dorothy.

front: Picture: a small child in orange footie pajamas with a burlap sack over his head that has button eyes and a stitched mouth, carrying a lollipop.
back: Sam, from Trick 'r Treat (2007, directed by Michael Dougherty). Under the sack he has a pumpkin-like head, and he punishes anyone who breaks the rules of Halloween.

front: In Trick 'r Treat, which grumpy old man, played by Brian Cox, gets a visit from Sam?
back: Mr. Kreeg, a Halloween-hating hermit who won't hand out candy.

front: Picture: black screen, opening credits in orange letters, and a lit jack-o'-lantern with a jagged grin as the camera slowly pushes in toward its eye. 1978.
back: The opening titles of John Carpenter's Halloween (1978), the film that introduced Michael Myers. Carpenter also composed the theme.

front: Picture: a green-suited villain on a bat-shaped glider, lobbing small orange jack-o'-lantern grenades.
back: The Green Goblin, Spider-Man's arch-enemy (Norman Osborn), with his trademark pumpkin bombs.

front: Picture: a cartoon of two brothers, one in a cape and a pointy red hat, in a village of skeleton-like people wearing pumpkin costumes, in an autumn-toned animated miniseries.
back: Wirt and Greg in Pottsfield, from Over the Garden Wall (2014, Cartoon Network, created by Patrick McHale).

front: Picture: a video game villager with a lit jack-o'-lantern for a head, a purple cape, and a candy-demanding attitude on October 31.
back: Jack, the self-proclaimed "Czar of Halloween," from Nintendo's Animal Crossing series.

front: Picture: a blocky orange cube with a carved, pixelated face. One version glows. It can be worn on the head.
back: The Carved Pumpkin and the Jack o'Lantern from Minecraft. Wearing a carved pumpkin keeps Endermen from turning hostile when you look at them.

front: In Minecraft, which two golems are built with a carved pumpkin as the head?
back: The Snow Golem (two snow blocks plus a pumpkin) and the Iron Golem (four iron blocks in a T shape plus a pumpkin).

front: Picture: in a tower-defense game, a large orange pumpkin shell placed over a pea-shooting plant, with the plant peeking out from inside.
back: The Pumpkin from Plants vs. Zombies (PopCap, 2009). It is a protective shell that goes over another plant.

front: Picture: a single emoji of an orange carved pumpkin with a triangle-eyed grin.
back: Jack-o-lantern emoji 🎃 (U+1F383), added in Unicode 6.0 in 2010.

front: Picture: a white Starbucks cup topped with whipped cream and a sprinkle of orange-brown spice. The drink has its own seasonal cult following and the hashtag #PSL.
back: The Starbucks Pumpkin Spice Latte, introduced in fall 2003. Product developer Peter Dukes led its creation.

front: Picture: a giant yellow fiberglass pumpkin covered in black polka dots, sitting at the end of a pier by the sea on a Japanese island.
back: Yayoi Kusama's Pumpkin (1994) on Naoshima Island, Japan (Benesse Art Site).

front: What happened to Yayoi Kusama's yellow Pumpkin on Naoshima in 2021?
back: A typhoon swept it into the sea on August 9, 2021, and it broke into pieces. A rebuilt version went back on the pier in October 2022.

front: Picture: a mirrored room full of glowing polka-dotted yellow-and-black pumpkins that reflect into infinity.
back: Yayoi Kusama's Infinity Mirror Room "All the Eternal Love I Have for the Pumpkins." Kusama is the Japanese artist famous for polka dots and pumpkins.

front: Picture: a 1990s album cover showing two young girls in fuzzy costume headbands, one with a star wand. The band's name contains a gourd.
back: Siamese Dream (1993) by The Smashing Pumpkins, the Chicago band fronted by Billy Corgan.

front: Picture: a double-album cover of a dreamy girl's face set inside a golden star against a blue sky. 1995. The band's name contains a gourd.
back: Mellon Collie and the Infinite Sadness (1995) by The Smashing Pumpkins. Its singles include "1979" and "Bullet with Butterfly Wings."

front: In what city were The Smashing Pumpkins formed, and in what year?
back: Chicago, in 1988, by Billy Corgan and James Iha.

front: Picture: a nursery-rhyme illustration of a man peering into a giant hollow pumpkin with a door and window, and his wife looking out.
back: "Peter, Peter, Pumpkin Eater." He "had a wife but couldn't keep her; he put her in a pumpkin shell, and there he kept her very well."

front: Picture: a young couple in a 1990s diner jumping onto the tables with guns: "Any of you pricks move, and I'll execute every one of you!"
back: Pumpkin (Tim Roth) and Honey Bunny (Amanda Plummer) robbing the diner in Quentin Tarantino's Pulp Fiction (1994).

front: In Pulp Fiction, what is Pumpkin's real name, as Jules calls him?
back: Ringo. Jules says, "Be cool, Honey Bunny," and calls Pumpkin "Ringo."

front: Picture: a hillside lit with thousands of glowing carved pumpkins arranged into shapes, including a Statue of Liberty and a carousel, at an 18th-century Hudson Valley estate.
back: The Great Jack O'Lantern Blaze at Van Cortlandt Manor, Croton-on-Hudson, New York, run by Historic Hudson Valley. It has about 7,000 hand-carved jack-o'-lanterns.

front: Which city holds the Guinness record for the most lit jack-o'-lanterns on display, and what was the number?
back: Keene, New Hampshire, with 30,581 lit jack-o'-lanterns on October 19, 2013, at the Keene Pumpkin Festival. It beat Boston's 30,128 from 2006.

front: Picture: a hugely lopsided, pale-orange pumpkin the size of a small car being hoisted by a forklift onto a giant scale at a California coastal festival.
back: The Safeway World Championship Pumpkin Weigh-Off in Half Moon Bay, California, the "Super Bowl" of giant pumpkins, held each October.

front: Whose 2,749-pound pumpkin set the world record at Half Moon Bay in October 2023?
back: Travis Gienger of Anoka, Minnesota. His pumpkin "Michael Jordan" weighed 2,749 lb (1,246.9 kg).

front: Who holds the Guinness-certified record for the heaviest pumpkin, as of mid-October 2026?
back: UK twins Ian and Stuart Paton, with "Muggle," 2,819 lb 4 oz (1,278.8 kg), weighed at Wargrave, England, on October 6, 2025. NOTE: in October 2026, Ian Paton reported 2,857 lb and Ron Wallace of Rhode Island reported 3,156 lb. Both were pending Guinness verification.

front: Who won the 2026 Half Moon Bay pumpkin weigh-off, and with what weight?
back: Travis Gienger of Anoka, Minnesota, on October 12, 2026, with a 2,389-lb pumpkin nicknamed "Rocky". It was his fifth Half Moon Bay title per Fox 9, though some outlets said fourth.

front: Which giant pumpkin variety are nearly all record pumpkins grown from, and who developed it?
back: The Atlantic Giant, developed by Howard Dill of Windsor, Nova Scotia.

front: According to Irish legend, who was "Stingy Jack"?
back: A trickster who fooled the Devil and was barred from both Heaven and Hell. He wanders the earth carrying a coal inside a carved turnip, and the name "Jack of the Lantern" became "jack-o'-lantern."

front: Before pumpkins, what vegetables were carved into lanterns in Ireland and Scotland?
back: Turnips, along with potatoes and beets. Irish immigrants in America switched to native pumpkins, which are bigger and easier to carve.

front: Picture: an old, gnarled carved turnip with a hollow grimacing face, displayed in a museum in Ireland.
back: A traditional Irish turnip jack-o'-lantern, the ancestor of the carved pumpkin, from the Samhain tradition.

front: Botanically, is a pumpkin a fruit or a vegetable?
back: A fruit, specifically a type of berry called a pepo. Pumpkins belong to the gourd family (Cucurbitaceae, genus Cucurbita).

front: Which Illinois town calls itself the "Pumpkin Capital of the World" and is home to a Libby's canning plant?
back: Morton, Illinois. Libby's processes most of the canned pumpkin sold in the US there.

front: Picture: a pumpkin catapulted from a giant trebuchet or air cannon, soaring across a field. The sport has a punny name.
back: "Punkin Chunkin," a pumpkin-launching contest best known from the World Championship Punkin Chunkin held in Delaware.

front: In the Peanuts special, which character skips trick-or-treating to wait with Linus in the pumpkin patch, and later demands restitution?
back: Sally Brown, Charlie Brown's little sister, who has a crush on Linus.

front: In The Nightmare Before Christmas, what is the name of Jack's home town and the doctor's ragdoll creation who loves him?
back: Halloween Town, and Sally, the ragdoll created by Dr. Finkelstein.

front: Picture: a short official in a tall striped top hat whose round head spins between a happy face and a worried face, wearing a "MAYOR" badge.
back: The Mayor of Halloween Town, the two-faced politician who leans on the Pumpkin King, from The Nightmare Before Christmas (1993).

front: Picture: a straw scarecrow riding a skeletal horse and holding a flaming jack-o'-lantern aloft, from the opening number "This Is Halloween."
back: Jack Skellington as the Pumpkin King, who sets himself on fire and dives into a fountain, in The Nightmare Before Christmas (1993).

front: Which annual Ohio event, held since 1903, is one of America's oldest pumpkin festivals?
back: The Circleville Pumpkin Show in Circleville, Ohio.

front: Picture: a cartoon pumpkin carriage turning back into a regular pumpkin on a road at midnight, with mice scampering away and a single glass slipper on the castle steps.
back: The end of the ball in Cinderella. The coach becomes a pumpkin, the horses become mice, and the prince keeps the glass slipper.
